why: The opacity ladder (design/w1b-opaque-statements.md), rule division: compound division in an integer file (a fraction where the model holds an integer). The translator reads its unit whole (the construct can make a value outside the model, the numeric boundary, or it is a declaration whose function value no step can output): the unit is one opaque function keyed by its source and the same-file units it reaches, and every same-file caller is one too, so no exact reading meets the value. same: one key on both sides, proved (not named unchanged, a Dafny keyword). escapes: a reordered return changes the source, another symbol, so the real reading does not prove it; the doubles reading reads the construct exactly and proves it (lane B: the same behaviour, PASS-bounded). caller: it reaches escapes, so it is opaque too in the real reading, and proved in the doubles reading; its record lists no site of its own.
